oracle.method: per node least-squares mechanisms in exact rationals, the abducted residuals as noise, the two-sided Gaussian tail by math.erfc, the Shapley value by enumeration of every order of the players, the members of each structure class enumerated by hand, and the weighted merge with its identified set and masses
oracle.formula: score(v) = -ln erfc(|v - c| / (s sqrt 2)); phi_j = average over player orders of v(S + j) - v(S) with v(S) the score of the target rebuilt from the noise of the players in S; change: v(S) = mean of the outcome in the model with the comparison mechanisms of S; class value = sum_m w_m phi^m / sum_{identified} w_m
asserted_outputs: cases.*.derived.merged (components, baseline, contributions, member_row_mean, lower, upper, identified_mass, unidentified_mass, total, contributions, tolerance, bayes.mean, bayes.sd)
context_only_outputs: draws and draw_sigmas (the stated Monte Carlo scale of the tolerance)
oracle.independence_basis: The generator rebuilds every table from the stated formulas, fits every mechanism by exact rational least squares, evaluates the Gaussian tail with math.erfc and the Shapley value by enumeration of the player orders, and imports no Antecedent code and no statistics package. The members of each structure class, their parents and their players are written by hand from the definitions (the DAGs of a Markov class, the completions of a PAG read as its most-confounded mixed graph, the districts of an ancestral sub-graph, a template repeated in every period of its window). Objects shared with the product: the stated lag alignment (a lagged column reads row max(t - L, 0)) and the stated convention that a contemporaneous edge of a template repeats in every period of the window; a misreading common to both would not be detected. The change allocation is exact at the mean level, so the product, which evaluates it by Monte Carlo, is held within 5 standard errors of its 2000 draws derived here; the Bayesian row-weight posterior is held to the closed-form moments of a Dirichlet(1, ..., 1) weighted mean.
oracle.historical_exposure: Written for this fixture from the stated definitions and the declared tables; the executing assertions were read to establish which values they compare, and no product implementation source was consulted to produce a number. The first run of the product against the derivation exposed a template convention (the contemporaneous edge repeats in every period) that the derivation was corrected to state, and a Bayesian posterior of a noise-block change attribution that ignored its row weights; the derivation was not changed for the second.

reference_review.redistribution: Repository-authored MIT OR Apache-2.0 generator and deterministic inputs. Python standard library only, in an isolated locked script environment, outside the product and ordinary CI; no upstream source is stored.
reference_review.limitations: Finite fixed tables, not sampling variability: the Monte Carlo of the change allocation is bounded by a derived multiple of its standard error, and the posterior moments are compared within the standard error of the draw count. The member enumeration is stated by hand per case, not generated. Calibration of the intervals is not measured.
